toolLevel.description: The identity level each tool needs: 0 anonymous, 1 the factors matched, 2 the factors and the one-time code. A tool without one needs the highest (fails closed). Every tool in rulesFor needs a row.

purposeLevel.description: The identity level each purpose needs (what a caller wants done before any tool is called). Default: none.

rulesFor.description: Per tool, the rules the gate runs before it, by id: the built-ins (R1 level, R2 scope, R3 confirmation, R5 role, R6 attempts, R7 service fields) or a custom rule the app's code registers. Every tool of the app needs a row; a tool without one cannot be called.

subjects.description: R2: per tool, the param that names the subject. A tool that runs R2 needs a row. Default: none.

param.description: The tool param that names the subject the call acts on.

via.description: "record" when the param is a record id the gate resolves to its owner; leave out when it is the subject's own id.

confirmedFields.description: R3: the fields a confirmed write carries, in the order the hash is taken over (for example name, dob, provider, date, time).

serviceFields.description: R7: per tool, the fields it may send on to a downstream service. A tool with no row sends none. Default: none.

maxAttempts.description: R6: failed attempts allowed at each identity check (the factors, the one-time code).

roles.description: R5: per tool, what each role of a principal that has one (for example depot staff) may do with it: allow, refuse, or person (a person takes the call). A tool or a role with no row is refused. Without the table, every role is refused.

rolePersonReason.description: R5's NEEDS_HUMAN reason when a role's access is "person" (for example "staff-filing"). Default "role-person".

scope.description: R2's description, by who asks and how the tool names its subject. Default: "The record belongs to someone this caller may see".

subject.description: R2's description when one of the app's subjects asks.

record.description: R2's description when the tool names its subject by a record id the gate resolves to its owner.

param.description: R2's description when the tool names its subject by the subject's own id.

delegate.description: R2's description when a party acting for subjects asks.

record.description: R2's description when the tool names its subject by a record id the gate resolves to its owner.

param.description: R2's description when the tool names its subject by the subject's own id.

recordOwner.description: What R2's compared line calls the owner of a record. Default "record owner".

subject.description: What R2's compared line calls a subject named by id. Default "subject".

role.description: R5's compared line for a role, by what the roles table gives it for the tool, as a template with {role} and {tool}.

allow.description: R5's compared line when the role may use the tool. Write {role} and {tool} where they go. Default "role {role} may {tool}: yes".

refuse.description: R5's compared line when the role is refused the tool. Default "role {role} may {tool}: no".

person.description: R5's compared line when a person takes the call. Default "role {role} may {tool}: with a person".

wording.description: The words the gate's built-in rules use in their description and compared lines, so the console and the audit read in the app's terms. Without it, neutral words.

description: policy.yaml: the gate's tables. Custom rule functions stay in code; this file only names them.
